title: Curve-preserving extrude with generated-chained selection produces disconnected geometry
description: Interactive role-play session hit this bug: the chain cube→cuts→assign_bezier_handles→inset_faces(sel)→extrude_mesh(selection=inset.generated, offset=-0.12, region=true)→coons_patch→merge_by_distance produces an OPEN mesh with floating disconnected cubes visible in the render (see ~/.ix/daud-interactive-friction-1/checkpoint-1.png). Dropping the extrude_mesh step and using deeper inset only restored watertight topology. Either (a) the ExtrudeMeshNode handle-preservation post-pass corrupts the surface when input handles exist, (b) the .generated BoolField is misaligned against inset.geometry's face indexing, or (c) coons_patch interprets corrupt handles on extruded edges non-manifoldly. Needs investigation with a reduced repro.
definition-of-done: 1. Root-cause identified (which of a/b/c). 2. Fix applied; the described DSL chain produces a watertight mesh with indented features. 3. Regression test added that exercises inset.generated→extrude_mesh chain under handles→coons_patch.
testing-plan: 1. Reduced repro: cube→handles→inset_faces on one face→extrude_mesh(selection=inset.generated, offset=-0.1, region=true)→coons_patch→merge. 2. Verify watertight output. 3. Verify no floating geometry. 4. Run full interactive skull DSL and confirm non-degraded similarity.
